name: Feasting Forest
body:
School evocation; Level druid 7, shaman 7

CAST

Casting Time 1 standard action
Components V, S

EFFECT

Range medium (100 feet + 10 ft./level)
Area 120-ft.-cube
Duration concentration, up to 1 round/level
Saving Throw see text; Spell Resistance no

DESCRIPTION

You instill a violent, bloodlust into the nature spirits and bring them to violence against your enemies.

Grasses, Undergrowth, Sand, Ice, Snow or Water. Any area within the affected area that is covered by such terrain becomes magical difficult terrain for your enemies and any creature passing through takes on 1d4 bleed. If a creature is currently bleeding from this terrain and moves through the area on another turn the bleed damage increases by 1.

Trees or other Large Plants: At the beginning of your turn, any enemy within 10 feet of a tree in the affected area takes 4d6 slashing or bludgeoning damage. A successful Reflex saving throw halves this damage. Any creature that fails their saving throw is also subject to an immediate grapple attempt by the trees. The trees have a CMB equal to your caster level + your spellcasting modifier + a size modifier for the tree’s size. Its CMD for the purposes of escaping the grapple is 10 plus its CMD.

Roots, Vines and Kelp: Any area with such plant material in the area acts as though under an black tentacles spell using this spell’s DCs.

Rocks, Ice or Crystals: As a free action on your turn, you can cause a loose chunk of such material to launch and strike an enemy within the area of the spell or 10 feet outside of its area. You make a ranged touch attack and on a hit, you deal 3d6 non-magical bludgeoning damage. Also on a hit, you can make a combat maneuver to trip the target using your spellcasting ability modifier instead of Strength.

If the spell deals damage, afterward, the affected area looks more verdant. When casting the spell you can designate a number of creatures that are not affected by the spell equal to your spellcasting ability modifier.
